titel: Reasons You Are Not Losing Weight On A GLP-1 | MMP Ep. 331

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: Why GLP-1 weight loss drugs fail and how underlying metabolic blocks prevent fat loss.
kurzfassung: Many women take GLP-1 medications to eat less, yet the scale still refuses to budge. This happens because the body has become poor at burning calories due to underlying factors like thyroid dysfunction, muscle loss, and chronic stress. Addressing these root causes through proper nutrition, resistance training, and nervous system regulation is essential for sustainable fat loss.
stichpunkte: GLP-1 medications reduce appetite and slow stomach emptying, but they do not fix an underlying inability to burn calories.
Caloric restriction significantly impairs the thyroid's ability to convert inactive T4 into active T3 hormone, slowing down metabolism.
Up to a third of weight lost on GLP-1s can come from lean muscle mass, which lowers resting metabolic rate and hinders long-term health.
Resistance training and adequate protein intake are non-negotiable to prevent muscle wasting and maintain metabolic health.
Chronic stress and elevated cortisol override GLP-1 effects by promoting fat storage in visceral abdominal tissue and raising blood sugar.
Poor sleep increases insulin resistance by up to 25% the following day and disrupts hunger and fat-burning hormones.
Nervous system regulation, such as deep breathing and reducing daily overstimulation, helps lower cortisol and reduce inflammation.
A structured step-by-step approach—prioritizing stress reduction, thyroid support, muscle building, and blood sugar stabilization—must precede any calorie deficit.

kapitel.titel: Introduction and the Core Problem with GLP-1s
Reason 1: Thyroid Hormone Conversion and Metabolic Resistance
Reason 2: Muscle Loss and the Importance of Strength Training
Reason 3: Cortisol, Stress, and Visceral Fat Storage
Practical Solutions for Sleep, Nervous System Regulation, and Stress
The Correct Order of Operations for Sustainable Fat Loss

clips.text: Taking medication to consume fewer calories without seeing any weight change indicates that calorie intake was never the root of the problem.

clips.hook: How calorie restriction cuts your fat-burning hormones in half
clips.text: Short-term caloric restriction drastically reduces the body's ability to convert inactive thyroid hormone into the active form needed for fat burning by up to fifty percent.

clips.hook: The hidden muscle loss behind weight loss drugs
clips.text: Clinical data indicates that approximately one-third of the weight shed while using GLP-1 medications consists of metabolically active lean muscle rather than fat.

clips.hook: How one bad night of sleep sabotages your metabolism
clips.text: Experiencing a single night of poor sleep can elevate insulin resistance by up to twenty-five percent the following day while worsening inflammation.

clips.hook: You cannot drug your way out of a broken metabolism
clips.text: Relying solely on pharmaceutical drugs cannot fix a body whose metabolic machinery is suppressed by chronic stress, inflammation, and hormonal imbalances.

You went on a GLP-1. You ate less. Your appetite disappeared. And the scale didn't budge. In this episode, Stephanie Crassweller breaks down the four scientifically backed reasons a GLP-1 fails to produce fat loss in women in perimenopause and menopause — and why three of them are things the drug actually makes worse.

If eating less was the fix, the drug would have fixed it. It didn't. Which means something else is blocking your body from burning — and Stephanie walks you through exactly what it is, what to test, and the order to fix it.
